newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-OSBORNE BACK AS FIRST CHOICE LEFT WING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-OSBORNE BACK AS FIRST CHOICE LEFT WING.

text.p: DUNEDIN, Aug 13 - Glen Osborne regained his spot in the All Black starting lineup on Wednesday and ends yet another test rugby season as the No 1 No 11, NZPA reports.
He is the only change to the team for Saturday's Tri-series and Bledisloe Cup test against the Wallabies at Carisbrook.

All Black coach John Hart denied that form influenced Osborne's selection ahead of Tana Umaga, who played in all the tests this season except in Melbourne, where he was still nursing a sternum and shoulder injury he suffered a week earlier at Ellis Park, South Africa.
Osborne started the match then and Hart described his game there as "sensational" after analysing it on video.
"It's no reflection on Tana Umaga. He's given us excellent service," Hart said.
"It was a case of either or. We've got two terrific left wingers and Osborne's worked so hard in all the time he's spent on the reserves this year."
Hart has never dropped a player from his test lineup unless form warranted him to do so, and he's done that only twice since he took on the coach's job last year.

However, with both wingers in equally good form, the selectors appeared to have swayed Osborne's way to reward him for his unerring commitment despite being in the reserve squad mostly this year and because there is still a little doubt about Umaga's injury.
Nevertheless, Osborne's promotion makes him the first-choice test left winger, a position he established last season after Jonah Lomu stuggled with a knee injury.
